## What it is

Kiwix serves **offline copies of Wikipedia and other reference works** to any browser on the home network. Each book is one ZIM file: a compressed archive of the articles plus a full-text search index ([kiwix/kiwix-tools](https://github.com/kiwix/kiwix-tools), [kiwix-serve](https://wiki.kiwix.org/wiki/Kiwix-serve)). It is the library of the **Offline Knowledge** bundle (`apps/_bundles/offline-knowledge/`, REC-NOMAD-01), and Library Chat answers questions from it.

**Licence:** `GPL-3.0` ([COPYING at 3.8.2](https://github.com/kiwix/kiwix-tools/blob/f76e38bdc06b86b73ba8e84a5de234a0d6c3fa3d/COPYING)). It is class **L2** (copyleft): it ships as its own container next to OneMind's Apache-2.0 code and is never linked into it (license-matrix row "Kiwix tools / kiwix-serve" [C-LIC-054]). **Content has its own licence:** Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0. Some other ZIM files on the Kiwix mirror are non-commercial, so the owner chooses them and OneMind never preloads them (license-matrix rows "Content: …").

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`) with two containers that share the 64 GiB volume `kiwix-data` (`/data`). Both use the image's own user (UID 1001), with a read-only root filesystem, no privilege escalation and all capabilities dropped.
- **`kiwix-serve`** serves every book in `/data/library.xml` on port 8080, with `--monitorLibrary`, so it picks up a new library without a restart. It starts with an empty library, so the page loads before any book is downloaded.
- **`library-sync`** is the **library manager**: [`manifests/library-sync.sh`](manifests/library-sync.sh), run at start and then every 6 hours. For each book in the owner's `zims` setting it:
  1. accepts only `<folder>/<file>.zim` (no URL, no `..`);
  2. checks the size on the mirror against the free space, keeping `reserve_mb` free;
  3. downloads with resume (`wget -c`);
  4. compares the file with the mirror's `.sha256` file and throws it away on a mismatch;
  5. rebuilds `library.xml` from exactly the listed books (`kiwix-manage add`).
  It never deletes a ZIM file. A book left out of the list simply stops being served.
- Settings (contract §12.22, delivered as ConfigMap `onemind-settings`): `zims` (the book list), `mirror` (an `https://` Kiwix mirror; checksums still come from that mirror) and `reserve_mb`.
- Backups keep the library list and skip the ZIM files (`*.zim`), which can be downloaded again.
- Other apps reach it at `http://kiwix.app-kiwix.svc.cluster.local:8080`. Its search API (`/search?pattern=…&format=xml`) is what Library Chat uses.

## First run

Source: [kiwix-serve](https://wiki.kiwix.org/wiki/Kiwix-serve) and the [Kiwix library](https://library.kiwix.org) (the catalogue of books with their sizes).

1. Install Kiwix from the Market, or install the whole Offline Knowledge bundle, and approve the action. It installs into `app-kiwix` with one small default book (climate change, 12 MiB) so you can try it at once.
2. Open it:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-kiwix port-forward svc/kiwix 8090:8080
   ```
   then go to http://localhost:8090.
3. Choose your books. Browse [download.kiwix.org/zim](https://download.kiwix.org/zim/) (or [library.kiwix.org](https://library.kiwix.org) for sizes). Then set the app's **Books** setting to the paths you want, separated by spaces, for example `wikipedia/wikipedia_en_all_mini_2026-09.zim wikivoyage/wikivoyage_en_all_nopic_2026-09.zim`. This is an `app.configure` action, which you approve. The library manager downloads and checks them, and each book appears when it is verified. Follow progress with `kubectl -n app-kiwix logs deploy/kiwix -c library-sync -f`.

**Sizes to plan for:** English Wikipedia "mini" (the intro of every article) is about 14 GiB; "nopic" (full text, no pictures) about 50 GiB; with pictures about 110 GiB. The volume is 64 GiB.

### Remove a book

Take it out of the **Books** setting, which stops serving it. Then delete the file to free its space:
`kubectl -n app-kiwix exec deploy/kiwix -c library-sync -- rm /data/<file>.zim`

## Not done yet

- **Disk size:** k3s local-path does not enforce the 64 GiB request. The library manager checks free space itself, but a bigger library needs a bigger disk, not a setting.
- **Supply chain:** upstream's image build downloads the kiwix-tools binaries over plain HTTP (`docker/Dockerfile` at 3.8.2, with `curl -k`). The bytes OneMind runs are fixed by the image digest and scanned by the gate, but the build itself is not reproducible from source. This is worth an upstream issue.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: the web UI is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists.
- No per-app login: anyone who can reach the page can read the library. That is acceptable for a read-only library; changing the book list needs the owner (it is a setting).
